name: Euston
source: Bureau of Meteorology, Water Data Online (KiWIS API)
datum: m, water surface elevation (values near the 47.6 m full supply level of Euston Weir; most likely m above the Australian Height Datum, but BoM does not say)
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0), per BoM Water Data Online copyright notice. Credit: Bureau of Meteorology, Water Data Online, with data supplied by the station owner (see notes).
notes: BoM series DMQaQc.Merged.DailyMean.24HR, ts_id 267468010, station_id 2877981 (station 414203 MURRAY @ EUSTON). Data owner: VIC - Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action.

Daily mean of the merged quality-controlled level record, aggregated by BoM to a 24-hour mean. The API does not say how many readings fed each early-year mean; where only one staff reading a day was taken, the 'mean' is that one reading.

Quality codes ({10: 'quality-A best available Quality', 90: 'quality-B compromised', 110: 'quality-C estimate'}): counts {10: 17721, 90: 45, 110: 897}. Mapping: A (10) and B (90, compromised) -> measured; C (110, estimate) -> estimated; E (140, unknown quality) -> measured before 1991 and provisional from 1991 on (0 days), where it marks recent unchecked readings.
Unknown-quality code E (140) share of days by decade: none.
Compromised code B (90) share of days by decade: {1990: 0.003, 2000: 0.0, 2010: 0.002, 2020: 0.01}.
17 empty timestamps (code -1) and 0 values coded F (210, missing or incorrect) were dropped.

measurement_history.fact: Euston Weir (Lock 15) was finished in 1937; its full supply level is 47.6 m and parts of it are removed during floods.
Data check: record starts with several readings a day. Values are water surface elevations near the weir level (about 42 to 52 m), not a local gauge height.
BoM lists two station entries for 414203 about 2.7 km apart; not explained. This file uses the entry that holds the daily mean series (station_id 2877981).
Many values carry quality C (estimate); 32% of days in the 1970s are estimated.
Not found: whether the gauge is above or below the weir, the datum name, gauge move dates, telemetry start.

public_notes: Euston sits at a weir, and parts of the weir are removed during floods, so we expect the level here to depend partly on how the weir is run. The numbers appear to be water surface elevations near the weir's 47.6 m full supply level, not heights above a local gauge; BoM does not name the datum. About a third of days in the late 1970s were estimated.
